name: Kery tester benchmark — complex UI, known planted bugs
note: Each case runs the real engine against a locally served app. detect[] are regexes ALL of which must match one finding (or one contradicted verification) for the bug to count as caught. Keep them behaviour-based, not wording-specific.

cases.intent: This page estimates shipping and discounts for a $42.00 cart. Work through these checks in order and record exactly what you observe for each: 1. Read the Subtotal, Shipping and Order total, then confirm the arithmetic: order total must equal subtotal minus any discount plus shipping. 2. Apply the promo code SAVE10 and check the Discount line equals exactly 10% of the SUBTOTAL (not of subtotal plus shipping) — state both numbers. 3. With SAVE10 still applied, apply an obviously invalid code such as NOTREAL; confirm the invalid-code error appears AND that the previous discount is removed rather than silently kept. 4. Select the Express tier and re-check that the order total updates consistently with the shipping price shown on that row. 5. Compare the FREE badge shown on a shipping row against the Shipping amount used in the totals — they must agree.
cases.context: New shipping estimator with delivery tiers, free-shipping thresholds, promo codes and a totals rollup.

plantedBugs.note: discount = (subtotal + tier price) * pct instead of subtotal * pct
plantedBugs.symptom: The discount amount shown is larger than the stated percentage of the subtotal, because shipping was included in the discount base.

plantedBugs.note: badge uses >= but totals use > for the free threshold
plantedBugs.symptom: A shipping row shows FREE while the totals still charge for that shipping (or vice versa) at exactly the threshold amount.

plantedBugs.note: invalid code sets an error but leaves the previous promo applied
plantedBugs.symptom: After applying an invalid promo code, an error appears but the previously applied discount is still shown/applied.

cases.prBody: Adds a public shipping estimator with delivery tiers, free-shipping thresholds, promo codes and a live totals rollup.

cases.intent: This is a 3-step onboarding wizard. Work through these checks in order and record exactly what you observe for each: 1. On step 1 press Continue with everything empty and confirm each required field shows an error. 2. Enter an email with NO dot in the domain, for example sam@example (plus a valid workspace name and display name), press Continue, and record whether the wizard accepts it — a malformed email must be rejected. 3. On step 2 pick a focus area, then set 'Max notes per day' to 25 and press Continue; the field states the allowed range is 1 to 20, so 25 must be rejected — record what happens. 4. On step 3 add three notes with DISTINCT text (for example 'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma'), then remove the SECOND one and record exactly which note text disappeared and which remain. 5. Finish and confirm the summary's note count matches the number of notes you actually left in the list.
cases.context: New public onboarding wizard collecting workspace profile, planning preferences and first notes, with per-step validation.

plantedBugs.note: regex dropped the dot requirement so sam@example passes
plantedBugs.symptom: An email address with no dot in the domain (e.g. sam@example) is accepted and the wizard advances, instead of showing a validation error.

plantedBugs.note: range says 1-20 but only the lower bound is enforced
plantedBugs.symptom: A daily limit above the stated maximum of 20 (e.g. 25) is accepted and the wizard advances, despite the label saying 1-20.

plantedBugs.note: remove uses slice(0,-1) so the last row goes, not the clicked one
plantedBugs.symptom: Clicking remove on a specific note removes a different note (the last one) instead of the one clicked.

cases.prBody: Adds a public three-step onboarding wizard collecting workspace profile, planning preferences and first notes, with per-step validation.

cases.intent: This page compares LLM models with filters, sortable columns and a monthly cost estimate. Work through these checks in order and record exactly what you observe for each: 1. Note the 'Showing N of M models' counter and count the visible table rows — they must agree. 2. Tick 'Vision only', then re-count the visible rows AND re-read the counter; they must still agree. 3. Click the 'Input $/1M' column header twice and record the first and last row each time — the second click must reverse the order. 4. Set 'Input M tokens / mo' to 10 and 'Output M tokens / mo' to 0, then verify one row's 'Est. monthly' by hand: it must equal the row's Input $/1M multiplied by 10. State the row, the input rate and the estimate. 5. Confirm the row tagged 'cheapest' really has the lowest Est. monthly of the visible rows.
cases.context: New public model comparison table with provider/vision filters, sortable price and context columns, and a usage-based monthly cost estimate.

plantedBugs.note: counter only accounts for the provider filter
plantedBugs.symptom: The 'Showing N of M models' counter does not match the number of table rows actually visible after filtering.

plantedBugs.note: arrow toggles but numeric comparator never inverts
plantedBugs.symptom: Clicking a numeric column header a second time flips the arrow but the row order does not actually reverse.

plantedBugs.note: monthly = outputRate*inM + outputRate*outM
plantedBugs.symptom: The estimated monthly cost is higher than input-rate x input-tokens, because the output rate is applied to input tokens.

cases.prBody: Adds a public model comparison table with provider/vision filters, sortable columns and a usage-based monthly cost estimate.

cases.note: HELD OUT. Never inspect per-bug results while tuning prompts — this case exists solely to detect overfitting to the other three. Run with --reveal only for final validation.
cases.intent: This page lists seat licence plans across multiple pages, lets you set a team size that can be remembered between visits, and lets you request a quote for a selected plan. Work through these checks in order and record exactly what you observe for each: 1. On page 1, note the name of every plan row. Click Next and note every plan row on page 2 — no plan may appear on both pages. 2. Tick 'Remember my team size', set the team size to 37, then reload the page and record whether the team size is still 37 and whether the checkbox is still ticked. 3. Without selecting any plan, check whether the 'Request quote' button is clickable; it must be disabled until a plan is chosen. If it is clickable, click it and record what the confirmation says. 4. Select a Business plan with a team size below its stated 'Seats from' minimum and record whether the warning appears and whether the button is disabled. 5. Select a plan and confirm 'Estimated monthly' equals that plan's per-seat price multiplied by the seat count — state all three numbers.
cases.context: New public seat licence planner with a paginated plan table, a remembered team size, and a quote request form.

plantedBugs.note: page 2 slice starts one row early so the last row of page 1 repeats
plantedBugs.symptom: A plan shown as the last row of page 1 appears again as the first row of page 2.

plantedBugs.note: writes purchasify.licences.seats but reads purchasify.seats
plantedBugs.symptom: After ticking remember and reloading, the team size reverts to the default instead of the saved value, and the checkbox is unticked.

plantedBugs.note: disabled uses meetsMinimum which is true when nothing is selected
plantedBugs.symptom: The Request quote button is clickable with no plan selected and submits a quote with no plan.

cases.prBody: Adds a public seat licence planner: paginated plan catalogue, team size that can be remembered between visits, and a quote request for the selected plan.

cases.context: New three-step event registration wizard: contact details, attendees with ticket types, then promo codes and totals.
cases.prBody: Adds a three-step registration flow: contact details, attendee list with ticket types, promo codes and a totals summary.

plantedBugs.note: option label advertises $260 but TICKET.workshop is 240
plantedBugs.symptom: The Workshop ticket is advertised at $260 in the dropdown but the subtotal charges $240 for it.

plantedBugs.note: stepping back from step 2 to step 1 clears state.attendees
plantedBugs.symptom: Going back from the attendees step to contact details and returning shows an empty attendee list; the entered attendees are lost.

plantedBugs.note: seats is validated but never used in pricing or confirmation
plantedBugs.symptom: The 'Seats reserved' field is required and validated but changing it never affects the totals or the confirmation message.

cases.context: New support ticket queue with priority and text filters, an open-only toggle, row selection and a bulk close action.
cases.prTitle: Feature: support queue with bulk actions
cases.prBody: Adds a filterable support ticket queue with row selection and a bulk close action.

plantedBugs.note: header checkbox selects every ticket, not just visible ones
plantedBugs.symptom: With a filter applied showing 3 rows, ticking the header select-all reports 8 selected — it selects rows that are filtered out.

plantedBugs.note: closeSelected never clears state.selected
plantedBugs.symptom: After closing the selected tickets the selection count stays the same instead of resetting to zero.

plantedBugs.note: toast reports selected count including already-closed tickets
plantedBugs.symptom: The confirmation says it closed N tickets counting ones that were already closed, so the number exceeds what actually changed.

cases.context: New inventory movement screen: record received and shipped quantities, undo the last movement, with low-stock flagging against a reorder point.
cases.prBody: Adds an inventory adjustment screen recording received and shipped stock, an undo for the last movement, and low-stock flagging against each item's reorder point.

plantedBugs.note: undo always subtracts, so undoing a shipment decrements twice
plantedBugs.symptom: Undoing a shipment lowers the stock again instead of restoring it; the quantity ends further from the original than before the undo.

plantedBugs.note: isLow uses < though the page says 'at or below'
plantedBugs.symptom: An item whose stock exactly equals its reorder point shows OK, though the page states items at or below the reorder point are flagged low.

plantedBugs.note: guard uses >= so shipping the full on-hand amount is refused
plantedBugs.symptom: Shipping exactly the quantity on hand is refused with a message saying that many are on hand.

cases.intent: This is an account settings form. Work through these checks and record exactly what you observe: 1. Press 'Save changes' with every field empty and describe what visibly happens on screen — any validation message must be VISIBLE to a sighted user, not merely present in the DOM. 2. Describe how each text input is labelled: state whether a persistent visible label exists, or only placeholder text that disappears once you type. 3. Fill in a valid name and email, press Save, and describe what the interface shows between the click and the confirmation — state whether the button changes, disables, or gives any progress feedback, and roughly how long the wait is.
cases.context: New account settings screen with profile fields, notification preferences and a save action.
cases.prBody: Adds an account settings screen where users update their profile and notification preferences.

plantedBugs.note: validation message positioned at left:-9999px so it is never visible
plantedBugs.symptom: Submitting with empty required fields appears to do nothing: the validation message exists but is positioned off-screen so the user sees no feedback at all.

plantedBugs.note: inputs use placeholder only, no label or aria-label
plantedBugs.symptom: The profile inputs have no visible or accessible label, only placeholder text that vanishes once the user types, leaving fields unidentifiable.

plantedBugs.note: save takes ~2.6s with no spinner, no disabled state, no message
plantedBugs.symptom: After pressing Save the interface shows nothing at all for around three seconds — no spinner, no disabled button, no message — so the action appears to have failed.

cases.intent: This is a weekly report page. Work through these checks and record exactly what you observe: 1. Read the small comparison text under each headline number (for example the '+12% vs last week' line) and state whether it is comfortably legible against the white card, or too faint to read. 2. Read the 'Summary of the week' cell for the first agent and state whether the full sentence is readable or visibly cut off mid-sentence, and whether any indication such as an ellipsis or expand control is offered. 3. Scroll to the very bottom of the page and state whether the fixed bar holding 'Export CSV' and 'Send to stakeholders' covers any table content.
cases.context: New weekly report screen with summary statistics, a per-agent table and export actions.
cases.prBody: Adds a weekly report with headline statistics, a per-agent summary table and export actions.

plantedBugs.note: #d8d8dc on white is a 1.42:1 contrast ratio
plantedBugs.symptom: The comparison text under each statistic is so light against the white card that it is effectively unreadable; contrast is far below the accessible minimum.

plantedBugs.note: fixed 34px height clips ~217 chars with no ellipsis
plantedBugs.symptom: The per-agent summary text is cut off mid-sentence by a fixed row height, with no ellipsis or way to read the rest.

plantedBugs.note: fixed bar overlaps the last table row by ~27px at the bottom of the scroll
plantedBugs.symptom: The fixed action bar at the bottom sits on top of the final table row, hiding part of the last agent's data.

cases.intent: This is a stock audit screen. Work through these checks and record exactly what you observe: 1. Describe the size of the plus and minus stepper controls next to each count and state whether they are comfortably large enough to hit accurately, especially on a touch screen. 2. Move focus between the controls using the Tab key only and state whether the currently focused control is visibly indicated on screen. 3. Press 'Submit audit' to open the confirmation dialog, then try to close it — try a close button, the Escape key, and clicking outside the dialog — and state whether any of these dismiss it.
cases.context: New stock audit screen with per-item count steppers, a reset action and a submission confirmation dialog.
cases.prBody: Adds a stock audit screen for counting items against system quantities, with a confirmation dialog on submit.

plantedBugs.note: 16x16px controls, below the 24x24 minimum
plantedBugs.symptom: The plus and minus stepper controls are only about 16 pixels square, well below the minimum comfortable or accessible tap target size.

plantedBugs.note: outline:none on all focusable controls
plantedBugs.symptom: Tabbing through the page gives no visible indication of which control has focus, making keyboard navigation impossible to follow.

plantedBugs.note: no close control, no Escape handler, no backdrop dismiss
plantedBugs.symptom: The confirmation dialog has no close button and ignores both the Escape key and clicks outside it, leaving the user stuck with no way back to the page.
